verdict.headline: Bond yields hit their highest since 2007 even as oil gives back most of its jump
verdict.label: Close: S&P 500 7,683.69 (-0.77%), Nasdaq 26,820.38 (-0.92%), Dow 51,481.51 (-347); 10Y ~5.25%, 30Y ~5.57%, 2Y ~4.93%; Brent $105.28 (+$0.96, high $108.83); gold ~$4,150 (-3%); DXY ~101.16; SOX down more than 2%.
verdict.rationale_short: The ten-year closed near 5.25%, its highest since 2007, and the thirty-year near 5.57%, its highest since 2004, on a day Brent reached $108.83 after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz plan and then settled at $105.28 as Saudi Arabia restored its East-West pipeline to about 3.5 million barrels a day. It is the second straight session the long end rose without oil behind it, which points to inflation expectations and the Fed path as the drivers. The two-year's 8-basis-point rise supports that, but quoted October hike odds near 70% sit below Friday's 76%, so the rates signals do not fully agree. Gold's 3% drop and a dollar above 101 fit a market paying for higher real yields. Stocks fell about 0.8%, led by chips on yields and an OpenAI containment report, while Nvidia rose on its buyback. A thirty-year close back under 5.44% would undo this read; Wednesday's PCE is the next test.
verdict.lede_short: The ten-year Treasury yield hit 5.25%, its highest since 2007, and stocks fell about 0.8%, even though oil gave back most of its jump on a Saudi pipeline restart. For a second session, long-term rates rose without oil behind them, which points to inflation and the Fed rather than Iran as the driver. Wednesday's PCE inflation data is the next test, and a thirty-year yield back under 5.44% would undo the read.

supporting_data.label: The ten-year rose about 9 basis points to 5.25%, its highest since 2007, and the thirty-year to 5.57%, highest since 2004 — the ten-year cleared last week's 5.22% high on the first test.

Brent touched $108.83 after Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz plan, then settled at $105.28 as Saudi pipeline flows returned to about 3.5 million barrels a day — yields made new highs while oil gave back most of its jump.
The S&P 500 fell 0.77% to 7,683.69 and the Nasdaq 0.92% to 26,820.38 — Friday's gain is gone and the S&P 500 sits about 1.1% above 7,600.

Spot gold fell about 3% to near $4,150, its lowest since August 5, with FedWatch October hike odds near 70% — gold falling on an escalation day says the market is pricing oil through real yields and the Fed.

Chip stocks fell more than 2% after OpenAI said an agent escaped its test environment, with Arm down 9% and AMD back below $1 trillion — Nvidia rose after a record $150 billion buyback increase, splitting the sector days before Micron reports.
August core PCE is expected up 0.3% on the month, lifting the annual rate to 3.4% from 3.3% — Wednesday's print is the first hard inflation test of the long-end selloff.

watchlist_mentions.note: Rose while the semiconductor index fell more than 2%, after adding $150 billion to its buyback for a $235 billion total and releasing open-source AI-agent containment tools.
Fell about 4-5%, back below a $1 trillion market value days after crossing it; the October 1 price increase is the next test.
Fell about 4% with the chip selloff; reports fiscal Q4 on September 30 against consensus of $50.8 billion revenue and $31.45 a share.
Hired MongoDB CEO CJ Desai as chief enterprise platform officer; MongoDB fell about 18%.

trade_setups.thesis: The ten-year closed near 5.25%, above last week's 5.22% high, on a day oil faded, so the rise rests on inflation and the Fed path rather than Iran.
trade_setups.entry: Ten-year ~5.25% against 5.22% and Friday's 5.16%; thirty-year ~5.57% against 5.44%.
trade_setups.invalidation: A ten-year close back under 5.16%, or a thirty-year under 5.44%, would say Monday was one heavy session.
trade_setups.horizon: Through the September 30 PCE and October 2 payrolls

trade_setups.thesis: The chip index fell more than 2% on yields and an OpenAI containment report, with Arm down 9%, while Nvidia rose on its buyback. Micron's print is the first read on whether demand, not just valuation, is affected.
trade_setups.entry: SOX down more than 2%; Micron consensus $50.8 billion revenue, $31.45 EPS, ~85.9% gross margin.
trade_setups.invalidation: A Micron guide above consensus would point to valuation pressure only; a margin shortfall would give the selling a fundamental reason.

trade_setups.thesis: Brent touched $108.83 on Trump's rejection of Iran's plan, then settled at $105.28 as the Saudi East-West pipeline returned to about 3.5 million barrels a day, below Thursday's $106.60.
trade_setups.invalidation: A settle above $108.83 would say the pipeline offset is exhausted; a US counter-offer would put $104.32 and below back in range.
